text:
Predicates:
TransportsMultiplePassengers(x) ::: x can transport multiple passengers.
OneSeater(x) ::: x is a one-seater.
TeslaModel3(x) ::: x is a Tesla Model 3.
SingleSeatElectricCar(x) ::: x is a single-seat electric car.
SoloEV(x) ::: x is a Solo EV.
Car(x) ::: x is a car.
JohnsCar(x) ::: x is John's car.
Premises:
∀x (TransportxMultiplePassengers(x) → ¬OneSeater(x)) ::: If something can transport multiple passengers, then it is not a one-seater.
∀x (TeslaModel3(x) → TransportxMultiplePassengers(x)) ::: All Tesla Model 3 can transport multiple passengers.
∀x (SingleSeatElectricCar(x) → OneSeater(x)) ::: All single-seat electric cars are one-seaters.
∀x (SoloEV(x) → SingleSeatElectricCar(x)) ::: All Solo EV cars are single-seat electric cars.
¬TeslaModel3(y) → (¬TeslaModel3(y) ∨ ¬JohnsCar(y)) ::: If John's car is not a Tesla Model 3, then John's car is not a Tesla Model 3 or a single-seat electric car.
Conclusion:
SoloEV(johnsCar) ::: John's car is a Solo EV.
